question: A right prism has a base in the shape of a trapezium with parallel sides 10 cm and 6 cm, and height 4 cm. If the prism height is 15 cm, what is the volume?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Volume of Prism = Base Area × Prism Height

⇒ V = [1/2 × (Sum of parallel sides) × Base height] × Prism height

⇒ V = [1/2 × (10 + 6) × 4] × 15

⇒ V = [1/2 × 16 × 4] × 15

⇒ V = 32 × 15 = 480

**∴ The correct answer is 480 cm³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Parallel sides of the trapezium base (a, b) = 10 cm and 6 cm

Distance between parallel sides or height of base (h) = 4 cm

Height of the prism (H) = 15 cm

**Formula Used:**

Area of Trapezium = 1/2 × (Sum of parallel sides) × distance between them

Volume of a Prism = Area of Base × Height of Prism

**Calculations:**

⇒ Area of Trapezium Base = 1/2 × (10 + 6) × 4

⇒ Area of Trapezium Base = 1/2 × 16 × 4

⇒ Area of Trapezium Base = 8 × 4 = 32 cm²

⇒ Volume of Prism = Area of Base × Prism Height

⇒ Volume of Prism = 32 × 15

⇒ Volume of Prism = 480 cm³

**∴ The correct answer is 480 cm³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Volume of a Prism

The volume of any right prism is calculated by multiplying its base area by its height. Formula: **V = Base Area × Height**.

Total Surface Area of a Prism

The total surface area includes the lateral surface faces and the two parallel bases. Formula: **TSA = (Perimeter of Base × Height) + 2 × Base Area**.

Volume of a Pyramid

A pyramid tapers to an apex, making its volume exactly one-third of a prism with the same base and height. Formula: **V = 1/3 × Base Area × Height**.
